diagnostics.message:
[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Auto Scaling group can launch self-managed EKS nodes before the configured EKS access entry for their IAM role has been created. Make the group wait for the access entry so nodes do not attempt to join before their cluster authentication entry is available.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Auto Scaling group can launch self-managed nodes before the EKS access entry for their IAM role is created. Since that entry enables the nodes to authenticate with the cluster, order the group after the access entry (for example, with an explicit depends_on).

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Auto Scaling group can launch self-managed nodes before the EKS access entry for their IAM role exists. Make the ASG wait for the access entry so nodes can authenticate when they join the cluster.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.aws_launch_template.this` only orders itself after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this` (the built-in worker-node/CNI/registry policies). The user-supplied Node IAM policies created in `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional` are never ordered before the launch template, even though the explicit `depends_on` exists precisely to ensure all node policies are attached before nodes launch and pods assume permissions. When `var.iam_role_additional_policies` is non-empty, instances/pods can come up before those additional policies are attached. `depends_on` should list `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional` alongside `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this`; there is no attribute reference that can express this (the launch template cannot reference a policy attachment), so no data-dependency fix is offered.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_launch_template.this` only has `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this]`, but the node IAM role also gets policies attached via `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional`. There is no attribute reference or `depends_on` establishing that ordering, so the launch template (and the ASG/instances it feeds) can be created before the additional policies are attached to the role. Instances launched from this template then come up with a role missing those additional permissions — exactly the "premature access of policies by pods that depend on nodes" scenario the existing `depends_on` on `.this` was added to prevent. `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional` should be added to that same `depends_on` list.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The launch template has an explicit depends_on on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this to prevent instances from launching before the node role's IAM policies are attached (pods requiring permissions on create). However, it does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional, which attaches the user-configured additional policies (var.iam_role_additional_policies) to the same role. There is no attribute reference from the launch template to .additional (it only references the instance profile/role name), so instances launched by the autoscaling group can come up and join the cluster before the additional policies are attached, causing the same premature-access failure the existing depends_on is meant to prevent.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The launch template explicitly depends on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this to prevent nodes from booting before the base EKS policies are attached, but the additional policy attachments (aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional, one per entry in var.iam_role_additional_policies) are not covered by any dependency. Nodes launched from this template use the instance profile credentials, so pods requiring permissions granted by the additional policies can start before those attachments take effect, causing AccessDenied failures on create/destroy. The launch template should also depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional.
